problems.title: Two equal trigonometric ranges
problems.question: Which functions share a range: I |cos3x−3|, II cos3x−3, III cos²3x−3, IV |cos3x|−3?
problems.idea: Use the formulas below to reduce the problem to simpler quantities.
formulas: cos3x∈[−1,1]; cos²3x and |cos3x| both range over [0,1].

problems.title: Maximize two sines with a fixed sum
problems.question: Find max(sinx+siny) if x+y=π/3.
problems.idea: Use the formulas below to reduce the problem to simpler quantities.
formulas: sinx+siny=2sin((x+y)/2)cos((x−y)/2).
steps: It reduces to cos((x−y)/2), whose maximum is1.
For example x=y=π/6 attains it.

problems.title: A sine-cosine difference
problems.question: Evaluate cos15°−sin15°.
problems.idea: Use the formulas below to reduce the problem to simpler quantities.
formulas: cosθ−sinθ=√2cos(θ+45°).
steps: At θ=15° this is √2cos60°=√2/2.

problems.title: A prism whose counts form a geometric progression
problems.question: In a prism, numbers of faces, vertices and edges form a geometric progression. How many body diagonals does it have?
problems.idea: Use the formulas below to reduce the problem to simpler quantities.
formulas: For an n-gonal prism the counts are n+2,2n,3n; geometric condition (2n)²=(n+2)3n.
steps: This gives n=6. Each lower vertex connects by body diagonals to n−3 upper vertices.
Thus the count is n(n−3)=6·3.

problems.title: Angle in a square prism
problems.question: A regular square prism’s body diagonal makes 60° with the base. Find cos angle B₁DC.
problems.idea: Use the formulas below to reduce the problem to simpler quantities.
formulas: With base side a, base diagonal a√2, height h=a√2tan60°=a√6.
steps: DB₁²=2a²+h²=8a². The component of DB₁ along DC has length a.
The cosine is a/(a√8).

problems.title: A cotangent minus tangent
problems.question: Evaluate cot(π/8)−tan(π/8).
problems.idea: Use the formulas below to reduce the problem to simpler quantities.
formulas: cotθ−tanθ=2cot2θ.
steps: At θ=π/8, this is2cotπ/4.

problems.title: A signed half-angle cosine
problems.question: sinα=−12/13 and π/2<α<3π/2. Find cos(α/2).
problems.idea: Use the formulas below to reduce the problem to simpler quantities.
formulas: α must be in quadrant III, so cosα=−5/13 and α/2 lies in quadrant II.
steps: Take the negative root in quadrant II.

problems.title: A listed root of a cubic
problems.question: Which listed value solves x³−3x=3x²−1?
problems.idea: Use the formulas below to reduce the problem to simpler quantities.
formulas: The tangent triple-angle relation suggests simple tangent values; direct substitution is enough for a listed candidate.
steps: At x=−1 the left side is2 and the right side is2.

problems.title: Diagonal section areas of an oblique square prism
problems.question: A prism has square base; a lateral edge makes the same acute angle α with both adjacent base edges. Find the ratio of its smaller to larger diagonal section area.
problems.idea: Use the formulas below to reduce the problem to simpler quantities.
formulas: Resolve a lateral edge v=(u,u,h), with length L; u=Lcosα and h²=L²−2u².
steps: The two diagonal-section areas are proportional to h and L, because one base diagonal is parallel to the horizontal projection of v and the other perpendicular to it.
Their ratio is h/L=√(1−2cos²α).

problems.title: Direction cosines of a box diagonal
problems.question: A rectangular box diagonal makes angles α,β,γ with the three edges at its endpoint. What identity holds?
problems.idea: Use the formulas below to reduce the problem to simpler quantities.
formulas: For edges a,b,c and diagonal d, cosα=a/d,cosβ=b/d,cosγ=c/d.
steps: Pythagoras gives d²=a²+b²+c².
Divide by d².

problems.title: Maximum of a quadratic in cosine
problems.question: Find max(3sin²α+2cos²α+cosα).
problems.idea: Use the formulas below to reduce the problem to simpler quantities.
formulas: Set c=cosα: expression=3−c²+c=13/4−(c−1/2)².
steps: c=1/2 is allowed, so the upper bound is attained.

problems.title: A ratio of half-angle tangents
problems.question: Given tan((β−α)/2)=3sinα/(5−3cosα), find tan(β/2)/tan(α/2) where defined.
problems.idea: Use the formulas below to reduce the problem to simpler quantities.
formulas: Set t=tan(α/2),z=tan(β/2); sinα=2t/(1+t²),cosα=(1−t²)/(1+t²).
steps: The equation becomes (z−t)/(1+zt)=3t/(1+4t²).
Cross multiplication simplifies to z(1+t²)=4t(1+t²).
Thus z=4t; the requested defined ratio excludes t=0.

problems.title: Three cosine values
problems.question: Evaluate cos(2π/3)+cos(4π/3)+cos(5π/3).
problems.idea: Use the formulas below to reduce the problem to simpler quantities.
formulas: The values are −1/2,−1/2,1/2.
steps: Add them.

problems.title: Base area versus lateral area
problems.question: A right parallelepiped has all12 edges equal. Its diagonal-section areas are in ratio2. Find base area divided by lateral area.
problems.idea: Use the formulas below to reduce the problem to simpler quantities.
formulas: Its base is a rhombus with diagonal ratio2; sinθ=2d₁d₂/(d₁²+d₂²)=4/5.
steps: For edge length a, base area=(4/5)a² and lateral area=4a².
Divide.

problems.title: Equal-area oblique sections through a base diagonal
problems.question: Two planes through a right prism’s trapezoid base diagonal make angles30° and45° to the base and cut different lateral edges. Their section areas are equal. Find the smaller-to-larger base ratio.
problems.idea: Use the formulas below to reduce the problem to simpler quantities.
formulas: A plane figure’s projected area equals its area times the cosine of its inclination.
steps: The two projected triangles divide the trapezoid along a diagonal; their areas are in the same ratio as the parallel bases.
Equal spatial areas give projected area ratio cos45°/cos30°=√(2/3).

problems.title: A product of tangent sums
problems.question: α+β=45°. Find (1+tanα)(1+tanβ).
problems.idea: Use the formulas below to reduce the problem to simpler quantities.
formulas: tan(α+β)=1 implies tanα+tanβ=1−tanαtanβ.
steps: Expanding the product gives1+(tanα+tanβ)+tanαtanβ=2.
problems.answer: 2, where the printed expressions are defined.

problems.title: Two angles in a right triangle with three equal base pieces
problems.question: In right ABC, BC is the longer leg and AC=CD=DE=EB, with C,D,E,B consecutive. β=AEC,γ=ABC. Find sin(β+γ).
problems.idea: Use the formulas below to reduce the problem to simpler quantities.
formulas: Set the equal length to1: CE=2,CB=3,AC=1. Then tanβ=1/2,tanγ=1/3.
steps: Both angles are acute and their sum is below90°, so their sum is45°.

problems.title: All increasing intervals on a restricted domain
problems.question: Find the increasing intervals of y=sin(2x+2) for 0≤x≤5.
problems.idea: Use the formulas below to reduce the problem to simpler quantities.
formulas: The derivative is2cos(2x+2); increasing requires cos(2x+2)>0.
steps: The maximal closed monotonic intervals are [−π/4−1+πk,π/4−1+πk], intersected with [0,5].
The nonempty increasing pieces are [3π/4−1,5π/4−1] and [7π/4−1,5].
problems.note: The listed interval [(3π−4)/4,(5π−4)/4] is one valid increasing interval but omits the second portion of the stated domain.

problems.title: A large diagonal section of a hexagonal prism
problems.question: A regular hexagonal prism has height/base-side ratio √5/3. Find its largest diagonal-section area divided by lateral area.
problems.idea: Use the formulas below to reduce the problem to simpler quantities.
formulas: For side a and height h, largest diagonal section=2ah; lateral area=6ah.
steps: The given height ratio cancels from the quotient.

problems.title: Two inclined sections through a triangle midline
problems.question: A right prism has isosceles right triangular base with leg a and height a/4. Through a midline parallel to a leg, two planes inclined45° to the base cut sections. Find smaller-to-larger section area ratio.
problems.idea: Use the formulas below to reduce the problem to simpler quantities.
formulas: Both projected sections are strips of width a/4 on opposite sides of the midline; their area scaling by1/cos45° is equal.
steps: The strip toward the triangle’s vertex has endpoint widths a/2,a/4, so area=(a/4)(3a/4)/2=3a²/32.
The other strip has widths a/2,3a/4, giving5a²/32.
Their spatial-area ratio equals their projection ratio.

problems.title: Amplitude after double-angle substitution
problems.question: Find the maximum of 4tanα/(1+tan²α)−3(1−tan²α)/(1+tan²α).
problems.idea: Use the formulas below to reduce the problem to simpler quantities.
formulas: The expression is2sin2α−3cos2α, with amplitude √(2²+3²).
steps: Its maximum is√13. A maximizing angle has nonzero cosα, so the original tangent is defined.

problems.title: A product of four special-angle factors
problems.question: Evaluate sin18°cos36°sin54°cos72°.
problems.idea: Use the formulas below to reduce the problem to simpler quantities.
formulas: sin54°=cos36°, cos72°=sin18°, and sin18°cos36°=1/4.
steps: The product is (sin18°cos36°)².
For example sin18°=(√5−1)/4 and cos36°=(√5+1)/4 verify the identity.

problems.title: Find a double-angle sine from a sum
problems.question: sinα+cosα=1/2. Find sin2α.
problems.idea: Use the formulas below to reduce the problem to simpler quantities.
formulas: (sinα+cosα)²=1+sin2α.
steps: Thus1/4=1+sin2α.

problems.title: An altitude in an oblique prism base
problems.question: In oblique triangular prism ABCA₁B₁C₁, face CC₁B₁B is a rectangle and A₁ projects to K on BC. What must hold in base ABC?
problems.idea: Use the formulas below to reduce the problem to simpler quantities.
formulas: The lateral-edge vector is perpendicular to BC because that face is rectangular.
steps: Its component within the base is AK, since A₁ projects to K.
Projecting a vector perpendicular to BC into the base preserves its zero component along BC. Hence AK⊥BC.

problems.title: Largest lateral face from a normal section
problems.question: An oblique triangular prism has lateral edge1. The dihedral angle there is120°, and distances from that edge to the other two lateral edges are2 and3. Find the largest lateral-face area.
problems.idea: Use the formulas below to reduce the problem to simpler quantities.
formulas: A perpendicular cross-section has triangle sides2,3 with included angle120°. Lateral face area=lateral edge times the corresponding perpendicular distance.
steps: The third normal-section side has square2²+3²−2·2·3cos120°=19.
The three lateral areas are2,3,√19; the largest is√19.
